one_liner: Pure managed C# OpenType shaper and text layout engine; on .NET 10 it is within about 8% of native HarfBuzz overall, beating it on four of ten scripts.
what_it_does: SixLabors.Fonts loads TrueType, OpenType (CFF1/CFF2), WOFF/WOFF2, variable and color fonts and runs a full GSUB/GPOS shaper with complex-script shapers (Indic, Myanmar and the Universal Shaping Engine per the README; Hebrew and Thai/Lao shapers were added in 3.0.0). On top of that it does UAX #9 bidi, UAX #14 line breaking, measurement, hit testing and caret APIs. Since 3.1.0 (PR #550) shaping is a public API: fill a caller-owned TextShapingBuffer (text, direction, language, optional script, kerning mode), call the static TextShaper.ShapeRun(font, buffer) for one directional run or TextShaper.Shape for logical lines, and read back ShapedGlyph records (glyph id, string and grapheme index, advance, offset). It is not a drop-in for HarfBuzz: the API, units and glyph order differ.
how_it_is_fast: Shaping runs on a pooled ShapingScratch (borrowed per call from a scratch pool) and a caller-reused TextShapingBuffer, so the steady state allocates zero managed bytes. The internal ShapingBuffer keeps glyph records, a metrics stream and a positioning stream as parallel arrays, so the GSUB walks touch only narrow records. A 256-slot direct-mapped cache serves cmap glyph-id lookups and another serves glyph metrics. A glyph-set digest, an approximate membership filter like HarfBuzz's set digest, lets lookups that cannot match be skipped. PR #550 also lists per-lookup feature masks, streaming substitution in place of tail shifts on length changes, plan features collected once per plan, a cached USE decomposition table and direct lookup probes in the Indic shaper. The JIT matters a lot: the same code is 1.13x to 1.36x faster on .NET 10.0.10 than on .NET 8.0.29, while the HarfBuzzSharp rows gain only 1.04x to 1.12x (derived from page data).
when_to_use: .NET 8+ services or tools that must shape text with no native dependency: a pure managed assembly that is marked trimmable and needs no per-platform native assets.
Complex-script text on .NET 10, where the vendor's run puts it ahead of HarfBuzzSharp: Devanagari 1.20x faster, Balinese 1.13x, Myanmar Zawgyi 1.06x, Hebrew at parity (1.02x).

When you need more than shaping (bidi, line breaking, wrapping, measurement, hit testing, caret and selection geometry) from one library, rather than HarfBuzz plus ICU or FriBidi plus your own layout.
High-volume shaping of many short runs, where you can keep one TextShapingBuffer per thread and want no GC pressure.
Text rendering in the SixLabors ImageSharp.Drawing stack, which uses it as its text engine.
when_not_to_use: Native C or C++ code: it is a .NET library, not callable from C++ without hosting the CLR. Use HarfBuzz directly.

Latin, Arabic or Hangul-heavy workloads where raw shaping latency matters: on .NET 10 it is 1.17x (Latin), 1.27x (Arabic) and 1.64x (Hangul) slower than HarfBuzzSharp, and about 1.08x slower across all ten scripts (geometric mean, derived from page data).
On .NET 8 it wins only Balinese (0.96x) and is 1.01x to 1.97x slower on the rest (about 1.27x slower geometric mean, derived from page data).
Fonts that depend on Apple AAT tables (morx, kerx): AAT shaping is not supported (issue #551, open).
Companies with 1M USD or more annual revenue using it as a direct dependency in closed-source software: the Six Labors Split License then requires a paid commercial license.

integration.dependencies: none (the 3.1.3 nuspec lists no dependencies for its net8.0 asset)
integration.min_toolchain: .NET 8 for the released 3.1.x packages (net8.0 asset); the main branch now targets net10.0 only, so building from main needs the .NET 10 SDK even though the README still says .NET 8
integration.platforms: any platform with a .NET 8+ runtime (pure managed code, no native assets)
integration.thread_safety: TextShapingBuffer is documented as not thread safe (use one per thread). TextShaper is static and takes pooled scratch state per call. An exception when rendering text concurrently with HintingMode.Standard (issue #484) was fixed in 2025.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false: a different API (TextShapingBuffer plus TextShaper.ShapeRun returning ShapedGlyph), not hb_buffer/hb_shape; glyph ids and positions are meant to match HarfBuzz (PR #550 reports 4,851/4,851 HarfBuzz corpus cases passing), but the units and run order differ

gotchas: Units differ from HarfBuzz: ShapedGlyph advances and offsets are floats scaled by Font.Size / UnitsPerEm (point size, no DPI) in a Y-up system, while HarfBuzzSharp returns integer positions in the font's scale units. ShapeRun returns glyphs in reading order, while HarfBuzz emits right-to-left runs in visual order.
The script is inferred from the text unless you set TextShapingBuffer.Script; Zawgyi text must be forced with ScriptClass.MyanmarZawgyi, just as HarfBuzz needs the Qaag script tag.

The measured 3.1.0 code walked GPOS one glyph after every lookup instead of following the buffer cursor, so contextual positioning lookups could be reapplied to glyphs already consumed (seen with Segoe UI Emoji 1.70). PR #565 fixed this in 3.1.3 (2026-09-17). Use 3.1.3 or later; the fix was not re-benchmarked.

Robustness against malformed fonts is recent: 2026 fixes cover IndexOutOfRangeException in cmap format 4 and GSUB lookup type 2 (#510, #514), OverflowException loading a collection (#534), and stack overflows on self-referential composite glyphs (#537) and cyclic COLRv1 paint graphs (#560). Treat untrusted fonts with care.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other .NET shaper is catalogued. Pick this when you are on .NET and want no native HarfBuzz. In Rust, Parley (layout on HarfRust) or sigilbuzz cover the same ground, and in JavaScript text-shaper or rustybuzz-wasm compare against harfbuzzjs rather than native HarfBuzz.
verified_claims_summary: First-party PR #550 (merged 2026-07-30, shipped in 3.1.0) runs the public ShapeTextBenchmark under the BenchmarkDotNet Gate job (3 launches, 5 warmup, 15 iterations); BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8 is pinned in tests/Directory.Build.targets at the v3.1.0 tag, though the PR prints no version, CPU or OS. Each iteration shapes one short run per script (25 to 60 characters) from the same font file bytes with Fonts' ShapeRun versus HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1.1 (Reset, AddUtf16, GuessSegmentProperties, Shape), summing advances. On .NET 10.0.10 Fonts takes 0.83x to 1.64x HarfBuzz's time, faster on Devanagari, Balinese, Zawgyi and Hebrew (barely). On .NET 8.0.29 only Balinese is faster. The HarfBuzz side pays about five managed-to-native calls per shape, which weighs most on the sub-microsecond Hangul and Zawgyi rows; the same string is reshaped every iteration, so both sides' glyph caches stay hot.
status_note: Active (3.0.0 on 2026-05-12, then 3.1.0 to 3.1.3 between 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-17 on NuGet; last commit 2026-09-17). It is reference only, because it is C# and under the non-OSI Six Labors Split License (Apache-2.0 only for open-source use, transitive use, non-profits and companies under 1M USD annual revenue).
